nodes.name: Expectations and growth
nodes.statement_short: One round at most doubles (push, pull) or triples (push-pull) the expected informed set, giving exponential-in-$t$ first-moment bounds.
conclusions: After one round from $S$, $E|S'|\le2|S|$ (push, pull) and $E|S'|\le3|S|$ (push--pull)
Hence $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le t]\le2^t|S|/m$ (push, pull) and $3^t|S|/m$ (push--pull)
nodes.statement: After one round from $S$, $E|S'|\le2|S|$ (push, pull) and $E|S'|\le3|S|$ (push--pull), and $E[n-|S'|]=(n-|S|)(1-\frac1n)^{|S|}$, $(n-|S|)(1-\frac{|S|}n)$ and $(n-|S|)(1-\frac1n)^{|S|}(1-\frac{|S|}n)$. Hence $\Pr[T(|S|,m)\le t]\le2^t|S|/m$ (push, pull) and $3^t|S|/m$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: lem:rumor-lower-growth

nodes.statement_short: Sum exact per-node infection probabilities with $1-(1-1/n)^k\le k/n$, then apply the envelope lemma.
nodes.statement: Sum the exact probabilities of Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-protocol-conditions} over the uninformed nodes, with $1-(1-\frac1n)^k\le\frac kn$; then Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: One round of the final phase (Lemmas 39 and 49)
nodes.statement_short: Lower-tail bounds on the number of uninformed nodes after one round for push, pull and push-pull.
assumptions: $u=n-|S|$ and $u'$ the number of uninformed nodes after one round
conclusions: Push, at any level $4\le v\le u$: $\Pr[u'<v/e-v^{3/4}]\le v^{-1/2}$
Push--pull: $\Pr[u'<u^2/(2en)]\le4e^2n^2/u^3$
nodes.statement: Let $u=n-|S|$ and $u'$ the number of uninformed nodes after one round. Push, at any level $4\le v\le u$: $\Pr[u'<v/e-v^{3/4}]\le v^{-1/2}$. Pull: $\Pr[u'<u^2/(2n)]\le4n^2/u^3$. Push--pull: $\Pr[u'<u^2/(2en)]\le4e^2n^2/u^3$.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: lem:rumor-lower-round

nodes.statement_short: Chebyshev's inequality on the lower tail, using variance at most $u$ and the per-protocol expectation of $u'$.
nodes.statement: Chebyshev's inequality on the lower tail of $u'$, with $\mathrm{Var}[u']\le u$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-variance} with nonpositive covariances) and $E[u']\ge u/e$ (push, from $(1-\frac1n)^k\ge e^{-1}$ for $k<n$), $E[u']=u^2/n$ (pull), $E[u']\ge u^2/(en)$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Final phase of push (Theorem 38 for push)
nodes.statement_short: Push needs about $\ln u$ more rounds to inform the last $u$ nodes, with exponential tail.
assumptions: every $n$, every $S$ with $u=n-|S|$ uninformed nodes and every $t$
nodes.statement: For every $n$, every $S$ with $u=n-|S|$ uninformed nodes and every $t$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)\le t]\le1600\,e^{(t-\ln u)/2}$.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-lower-final-push

nodes.statement_short: Lower envelope along explicit targets $g_i=q_i^3(q_i-20)$, summing per-round failure probabilities from the one-round lemma.
nodes.statement: Lower envelope (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}) along the explicit targets $g_i=q_i^3(q_i-20)$, $q_i=(ue^{-i})^{1/4}$, which replace the paper's recursive $u_{j+1}=E_0(u_j)$ (Lemma~40). The step $g(qe^{-1/4})\le g(q)/e-g(q)^{3/4}$ reduces to $c^4-20c+20\le0$ for $c=e^{1/4}$; while $q_i\ge40$, round $i$ fails with probability at most $2/q_i^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-round}) and these failure probabilities sum to at most $4e^{(t-\ln u)/2}$; when $q_t<40$ the bound exceeds $1$.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Final phase of pull and push-pull (Theorem 48 with l=2)
nodes.statement_short: Pull and push-pull cannot finish the final phase in fewer than $\log_2\ln n-5$ rounds except with probability $O(n^{-1/2})$.
assumptions: $n\ge3$, every $S$ with $2|S|\le n$ and every $t\le\log_2\ln n-5$
nodes.statement: For $n\ge3$, every $S$ with $2|S|\le n$ and every $t\le\log_2\ln n-5$: $\Pr[T(|S|,n)\le t]\le128\,n^{-1/2}$ (pull) and $128e^2n^{-1/2}$ (push--pull).
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-lower-final-double

nodes.statement_short: Lower envelope along double-exponential targets with the one-round lemma; weaker exponent $-1/2$ from a cruder variance bound.
nodes.statement: Lower envelope along the double exponential targets $g_i=2n(1/4)^{2^i}$ (pull) and $2en(1/(4e))^{2^i}$ (push--pull), the paper's $\varepsilon_{j+1}=E(\varepsilon_j)/2$, with Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-round}. The paper's exponent $-1+2\alpha\ell$ is replaced by the weaker $-1/2$, which comes from the cruder variance bound and suffices below.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Lower bounds for push, pull and push-pull (Theorems 51-53)
nodes.statement_short: Push, pull and push-pull from one informed node need $\log_2 n+\ln n$, $\log_2 n+\log_2\ln n$, $\log_3 n+\log_2\ln n$ rounds minus $O(1)$, with exponential tails.
assumptions: for $n\ge N$ and one informed node on $K_n$
conclusions: all nodes are informed within $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push), $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (pull) and $\lfloor\log_3n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push--pull) rounds with probability at most $Ae^{-\kappa r}$
the expected times are at least $\log_2n+\ln n-B$, $\log_2n+\log_2\ln n-B$ and $\log_3n+\log_2\ln n-B$
nodes.statement: There are $A$, $B$, $\kappa>0$ and $N$ such that, for $n\ge N$ and one informed node on $K_n$, all nodes are informed within $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push), $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (pull) and $\lfloor\log_3n\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-r$ (push--pull) rounds with probability at most $Ae^{-\kappa r}$; the expected times are at least $\log_2n+\ln n-B$, $\log_2n+\log_2\ln n-B$ and $\log_3n+\log_2\ln n-B$ (stated for every partial sum $\sum_{t<R}\Pr[T>t]$ with $R$ at least the bound).
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull
nodes.label: thm:rumor-protocols-lower

nodes.statement_short: Join growth and final phases at a fixed time with $m'=n/2$: growth bounded by first moment, final phase by the final-phase theorems; sum tails for expectations.
nodes.statement: Join the two phases at a fixed time (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}) with $m'=n/2$. Push: after $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor-\lceil r/2\rceil$ rounds at most $n/2$ nodes are informed except with probability $O(2^{-r/2})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-growth}), and from there Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-push} bounds the rest. Pull and push--pull: the same with $\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-5$ rounds for the final phase (Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-double}), whose $n^{-1/2}$ becomes $e^{-(\ln2/4)r}$ since a nontrivial time forces $r\le2\log_2n$. The tails have rate $\kappa=\ln2/4$; the expectations follow by summing the tail series.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Join phases
nodes.statement: Join the two phases at a fixed time (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-generic}) with $m'=n/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Join the two phases at a fixed time with $m'=n/2$.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Push case
nodes.statement: Push: after $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor-\lceil r/2\rceil$ rounds at most $n/2$ nodes are informed except with probability $O(2^{-r/2})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rumor-lower-growth}), and from there Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-push} bounds the rest.
nodes.statement_short: Push: growth bound then final-phase theorem for push.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Pull and push-pull case
nodes.statement: Pull and push--pull: the same with $\lfloor\log_2\ln n\rfloor-5$ rounds for the final phase (Theorem~\ref{thm:rumor-lower-final-double}), whose $n^{-1/2}$ becomes $e^{-(\ln2/4)r}$ since a nontrivial time forces $r\le2\log_2n$.
nodes.statement_short: Pull/push-pull: same with the double-exponential final phase.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Tails and expectations
nodes.statement: The tails have rate $\kappa=\ln2/4$; the expectations follow by summing the tail series.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential tails with rate $\ln2/4$; sum the tail series for expectations.
nodes.section: 43 Rumor spreading revisited: lower bounds for push, pull and push--pull

nodes.name: Rounds of neighbour choices
nodes.statement_short: A round assigns each vertex $k$ neighbour samples; uniform rounds sample uniformly with replacement, independently per vertex.
nodes.statement: In a round $r$, every vertex $x$ of a finite graph $G$ samples $k$ neighbours $r(x,0),\dots,r(x,k-1)$. A uniform round is exactly the paper's sampling: $k$ uniform neighbours with replacement, independently for every vertex; $t$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds are averaged with \texttt{Dynamics.expList}. If $G$ is connected and has at least two vertices, rounds exist.
nodes.label: def:choices

nodes.statement: If $G$ is connected and has at least two vertices, rounds exist.
nodes.name: Rounds exist on connected graphs
assumptions: $G$ is connected and has at least two vertices
conclusions: rounds exist

nodes.statement_short: Connected graphs with at least two vertices have no isolated vertex.
nodes.statement: Every vertex of a connected graph with at least two vertices has a neighbour.

nodes.name: COBRA and BIPS
nodes.statement_short: COBRA pushes the active set to all sampled neighbours; BIPS with persistent source infects vertices that sample an infected vertex.
nodes.statement: COBRA from $C_0=C$: $C_{s+1}=\{r_{s+1}(x,i) : x\in C_s,\ i<k\}$. BIPS with persistent source $v$ from $A_0$: $A_{s+1}=\{v\}\cup\{u : \exists i,\ r_{s+1}(u,i)\in A_s\}$.
nodes.label: def:cobra

nodes.name: Time reversal of i.i.d.\ rounds
nodes.statement_short: Reversing the order of i.i.d. uniform rounds preserves expectations.
assumptions: every functional $F$ of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds
conclusions: $\mathbb E[F(r_T,\dots,r_1)]=\mathbb E[F(r_1,\dots,r_T)]$
nodes.statement: For every functional $F$ of $T$ i.i.d.\ uniform rounds, $\mathbb E[F(r_T,\dots,r_1)]=\mathbb E[F(r_1,\dots,r_T)]$.
nodes.label: lem:reverse

nodes.statement_short: Uniform average on $\mathrm{Fin}\,T\to\alpha$ is invariant under precomposition with reversal.
nodes.statement: The uniform average over $\mathrm{Fin}\,T\to\alpha$ is invariant under $\omega\mapsto\omega\circ\mathrm{rev}$ (the time-reversal lemma of the shared \texttt{dynamics} package).

nodes.name: Pathwise duality
nodes.statement_short: COBRA from $C$ hits $v$ along given rounds iff BIPS from $\{v\}$ along the reversed rounds infects a vertex of $C$.
conclusions: COBRA from $C$ along $r_1,\dots,r_t$ visits $v$ at some time $s\le t$ (time $0$ included) iff BIPS from $\{v\}$ along $r_t,\dots,r_1$ infects a vertex of $C$
equivalent_conditions: COBRA from $C$ along $r_1,\dots,r_t$ visits $v$ at some time $s\le t$ (time $0$ included)
BIPS from $\{v\}$ along $r_t,\dots,r_1$ infects a vertex of $C$
nodes.statement: For all rounds $r_1,\dots,r_t$: COBRA from $C$ along $r_1,\dots,r_t$ visits $v$ at some time $s\le t$ (time $0$ included) iff BIPS from $\{v\}$ along $r_t,\dots,r_1$ infects a vertex of $C$.
nodes.label: lem:pathwise

nodes.statement_short: Induction on $t$, generalizing $C$: both sides express a sampled chain from $C$ reaching $v$.
nodes.statement: Induction on $t$, generalizing $C$. Both sides say that a chain $x_0\in C$, $x_j=r_j(x_{j-1},i_j)$, reaches $v$ within $t$ steps: COBRA unfolds the first round, BIPS the last round of the reversed sequence.

nodes.name: COBRA-BIPS duality (Theorem 4 of Cooper-Radzik-Rivera)
nodes.statement_short: COBRA from $C$ fails to hit $v$ by time $t$ with the same probability that BIPS from $\{v\}$ misses $C$ at time $t$.
assumptions: every finite graph, every $k$, every vertex $v$, set $C$ and time $t$
conclusions: $\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_C(v)>t\mid C_0=C)=\mathbb P(C\cap A_t=\emptyset\mid A_0=\{v\})$
$\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_u(v)>t)=\mathbb P(u\notin A_t\mid A_0=\{v\})$
nodes.statement: For every finite graph, every $k$, every vertex $v$, set $C$ and time $t$: $\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_C(v)>t\mid C_0=C)=\mathbb P(C\cap A_t=\emptyset\mid A_0=\{v\})$. In particular (equation (2)), $\hat{\mathbb P}(\mathrm{Hit}_u(v)>t)=\mathbb P(u\notin A_t\mid A_0=\{v\})$. The paper assumes $G$ connected and regular and $k\ge1$; none of this is needed.
nodes.label: thm:duality

nodes.statement_short: Pathwise duality identifies the events after reversing rounds; time reversal preserves the law.
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:pathwise} identifies the two events after reversing the rounds, and Lemma~\ref{lem:reverse} says that reversing the rounds preserves their law. The paper proves the theorem instead by induction on $t$ with one-step conditioning.
Here $G$ is $r$-regular with $r>0$ on $n$ vertices, $P=A(G)/r$, $\lambda=\max(\lambda_2,|\lambda_n|)$, $k\ge2$, and $d_A(x)=|N(x)\cap A|$.
nodes.name: Setting for COBRA cover time: transition matrix and neighbourhood counts
Second eigenvalue
nodes.statement: $\lambda=\max(\lambda_2,|\lambda_n|)$ for the sorted eigenvalues of $P$ ($0$ if $n<2$).
nodes.label: def:lambda

nodes.name: Spectral core of Lemma 1
nodes.statement_short: Spectral bound on the squared normalized neighbourhood counts of a set $A$.
conclusions: $\sum_x (d_A(x)/r)^2\le\lambda^2|A|+(1-\lambda^2)|A|^2/n$
nodes.statement: For every set $A$: $\sum_x (d_A(x)/r)^2\le\lambda^2|A|+(1-\lambda^2)|A|^2/n$.
nodes.label: lem:crr-spectral

nodes.statement_short: Write the sum as $\|P1_A\|^2$ and expand in an orthonormal eigenbasis; trivial bound if $\lambda\ge1$.
nodes.statement: $\sum_x(d_A(x)/r)^2=\|P1_A\|^2$; expand $1_A$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis of $P$: the top eigenvector is constant with coefficient $|A|/\sqrt n$, and every other eigenvalue has square at most $\lambda^2$. If $\lambda\ge1$, use $d_A(x)\le r$ and $\sum_x d_A(x)=r|A|$.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 of Cooper-Radzik-Rivera: BIPS growth, MGF and Chernoff bound
nodes.statement_short: One BIPS round grows the infected set in expectation by a spectral factor, with an MGF bound and a Chernoff lower tail.
conclusions: $\E e^{-\varphi|A'|}\le\exp(-(1-e^{-\varphi})\E|A'|)$ for every real $\varphi$
$\Pr(|A'|\le(1-\delta)\mu)\le e^{-\delta^2\mu/2}$ for $\mu\le\E|A'|$, $0<\delta<1$
nodes.statement: One BIPS round from $A$ gives $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+(1-\lambda^2)(1-|A|/n))$, $\E e^{-\varphi|A'|}\le\exp(-(1-e^{-\varphi})\E|A'|)$ for every real $\varphi$, and $\Pr(|A'|\le(1-\delta)\mu)\le e^{-\delta^2\mu/2}$ for $\mu\le\E|A'|$, $0<\delta<1$.
nodes.label: lem:crr-growth

nodes.statement_short: Independent infections: bound each infection probability, sum with the spectral lemma; MGF factorizes, Chernoff via Markov.
nodes.statement: Vertices are infected independently; $u\ne v$ with probability $1-(1-d_A(u)/r)^k\ge 2d_A(u)/r-(d_A(u)/r)^2$. Sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}. The MGF factors over the vertices and $1-x\le e^{-x}$; the Chernoff bound is Markov's inequality with $\varphi=-\log(1-\delta)$.

nodes.name: Expected growth
nodes.statement: Vertices are infected independently; $u\ne v$ with probability $1-(1-d_A(u)/r)^k\ge 2d_A(u)/r-(d_A(u)/r)^2$. Sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound infection probabilities and sum with the spectral lemma.

nodes.name: MGF and Chernoff
nodes.statement: The MGF factors over the vertices and $1-x\le e^{-x}$; the Chernoff bound is Markov's inequality with $\varphi=-\log(1-\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: MGF factorizes; Chernoff via Markov's inequality.

nodes.name: Lemmas 2 to 4 of Cooper-Radzik-Rivera for an abstract growth process
nodes.statement_short: A monotone growth process with persistent source and MGF bound reaches $m$, then $9n/10$, then covers $V$ in $O(\log n/c^2)$, $O(\log n/c)$ rounds w.h.p.
assumptions: a round-driven set process have a persistent source, the MGF bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-growth}, growth $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+c(1-|A|/n))$ with $0<c\le1$, be monotone, and have $V$ absorbing
conclusions: From $\{v\}$ the size exceeds $m\le n/2$ within $13m/c+24C\log n/c^2$ rounds except with probability $n^{-C}$
from $|A_0|\ge4000\log n/c^2$ it reaches $9n/10$ within $T\ge24\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $T n^{-5}$
from $|A_0|\ge9n/10$ (if $4000\log n/c^2\le 9n/10$) it covers $V$ after $T\ge8\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $n^{-5}$
BIPS satisfies the hypotheses with $c=1-\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let a round-driven set process have a persistent source, the MGF bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-growth}, growth $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+c(1-|A|/n))$ with $0<c\le1$, be monotone, and have $V$ absorbing. From $\{v\}$ the size exceeds $m\le n/2$ within $13m/c+24C\log n/c^2$ rounds except with probability $n^{-C}$; from $|A_0|\ge4000\log n/c^2$ it reaches $9n/10$ within $T\ge24\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $T n^{-5}$; from $|A_0|\ge9n/10$ (if $4000\log n/c^2\le 9n/10$) it covers $V$ after $T\ge8\log n/c$ rounds except with probability $n^{-5}$. BIPS satisfies the hypotheses with $c=1-\lambda$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-phases

nodes.statement_short: Phase by phase: exponential supermartingale while small, per-round union bound with moving targets, then a recursion for healthy vertices.
nodes.statement: Lemma~2: the exponential supermartingale $e^{-\varphi|A_t|}$ on the event of staying small, $\varphi=\log(1+c/2)$. Lemma~3: a round with $|A'|<|A|(1+c/23)$ has probability $\le n^{-5}$; union bound over rounds with moving targets. Lemma~4: staying above $9n/10$ and the recursion $\E B_{t+1}\le\theta\E B_t+tn^{-7}$ for the number $B_t$ of healthy vertices. The paper's Lemmas~3 and~4 need minor corrections ($\log_2$ versus $\ln$ doublings; a missing factor $B_0$).

nodes.name: Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Lemma~2: the exponential supermartingale $e^{-\varphi|A_t|}$ on the event of staying small, $\varphi=\log(1+c/2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential supermartingale while the set is small.

nodes.name: Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Lemma~3: a round with $|A'|<|A|(1+c/23)$ has probability $\le n^{-5}$; union bound over rounds with moving targets.
nodes.statement_short: Per-round failure $\le n^{-5}$; union bound with moving targets.

nodes.name: Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Lemma~4: staying above $9n/10$ and the recursion $\E B_{t+1}\le\theta\E B_t+tn^{-7}$ for the number $B_t$ of healthy vertices.
nodes.statement_short: Recursion for the expected number of healthy vertices.

nodes.name: Corrections note
nodes.statement: The paper's Lemmas~3 and~4 need minor corrections ($\log_2$ versus $\ln$ doublings; a missing factor $B_0$).
nodes.statement_short: Notes minor corrections to the paper's Lemmas 3 and 4.

nodes.name: BIPS infection time on expanders (Theorem 2 of Cooper-Radzik-Rivera)
nodes.statement_short: On expanders BIPS infects all vertices within $O(\log n/(1-\lambda)^3)$ rounds w.h.p. and in expectation.
conclusions: BIPS from $\{v\}$ has $A_T\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^3$ for $T\ge60000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$
$\sum_{s<H}\Pr(A_s\ne V)\le 130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$
nodes.statement: If $1-\lambda\ge128\sqrt{\log n/n}$, BIPS from $\{v\}$ has $A_T\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^3$ for $T\ge60000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$, and $\sum_{s<H}\Pr(A_s\ne V)\le 130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-bips

nodes.statement_short: Chain the three phases at their hitting times; for the expectation restart from the current set using monotonicity.
nodes.statement: Chain the three phases at their first hitting times with $m=\ceil{4000\log n/(1-\lambda)^2}$ and $C=3$. (The paper's proof takes $m=4000\log n/(1-\lambda^2)$, which needs a minor correction: Lemma~3 needs $|A|\ge4000\log n/(1-\lambda)^2$.) For the expectation, restart from the current set: monotonicity and the persistent source give $\Pr(A_{s+T_0}\ne V)\le\Pr(A_s\ne V)/2$.

nodes.name: COBRA cover time on expanders (Theorem 1 of Cooper-Radzik-Rivera)
nodes.statement_short: COBRA covers an expander in $O(\log n/(1-\lambda)^3)$ rounds w.h.p. and in expectation.
conclusions: COBRA from $\{u\}$ has $\bigcup_{t=1}^T C_t\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^2$ for $T\ge60002\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$
every partial tail sum of the cover time is at most $130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$
nodes.statement: If $1-\lambda\ge128\sqrt{\log n/n}$, COBRA from $\{u\}$ has $\bigcup_{t=1}^T C_t\ne V$ with probability at most $3/n^2$ for $T\ge60002\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$, and every partial tail sum of the cover time is at most $130000\log n/(1-\lambda)^3$.
nodes.label: thm:crr-cobra

nodes.statement_short: Union bound over the missed vertex; duality reduces missing $w$ to BIPS not infecting everything; restart for the expectation.
nodes.statement: Union bound over the missed vertex $w$. Splitting off the first round, missing $w$ at the times $1,\dots,T$ is not hitting $w$ within $T-1$ rounds from $C_1\ne\emptyset$, which by Theorem~\ref{thm:duality} has probability $\Pr(C_1\cap A_{T-1}=\emptyset)\le\Pr(A_{T-1}\ne V)$. For the expectation, restart COBRA from the nonempty set $C_s$ (equation~(1)).

nodes.name: Union bound
nodes.statement: Union bound over the missed vertex $w$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a fixed missed vertex $w$.

nodes.name: Apply duality
nodes.statement: Splitting off the first round, missing $w$ at the times $1,\dots,T$ is not hitting $w$ within $T-1$ rounds from $C_1\ne\emptyset$, which by Theorem~\ref{thm:duality} has probability $\Pr(C_1\cap A_{T-1}=\emptyset)\le\Pr(A_{T-1}\ne V)$.
nodes.statement_short: Duality turns missing $w$ into BIPS not covering $V$.

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.statement: For the expectation, restart COBRA from the nonempty set $C_s$ (equation~(1)).
nodes.statement_short: Restart COBRA from the current nonempty set.

nodes.name: Branching factor 1+p/q
nodes.statement_short: Each vertex uses a second neighbour sample with probability $p/q$, giving COBRA/BIPS with branching factor $1+p/q$.
nodes.statement: A round gives every vertex two neighbour samples and a uniform coin in $\{0,\dots,q-1\}$; a vertex uses its second sample iff its coin is $<p$. COBRA pushes to the used samples, BIPS contacts them.
nodes.label: def:coin

nodes.name: COBRA with fractional branching factor (Theorem 4, Corollary 1, Theorem 3)
nodes.origin_citation: Cooper, Radzik, Rivera, PODC 2016 (Theorem 4, Corollary 1, Theorem 3)
nodes.statement_short: Duality and spectral growth extend to branching factor $1+\rho$; the cover time is $O(\log n)$ w.h.p. on expanders.
conclusions: The duality holds for the coin processes
the COBRA cover time with branching factor $1+\rho$ is at most $C\log n$ with probability $1-C/n^2$ and in expectation
nodes.statement: The duality holds for the coin processes; with $\rho=p/q$, $\E|A'|\ge|A|(1+\rho(1-\lambda^2)(1-|A|/n))$; and for constants $\lambda_0<1$, $\rho_0>0$ there are $C,N$ such that for $n\ge N$, $\lambda\le\lambda_0$ and $\rho\in[\rho_0,1]$ the COBRA cover time with branching factor $1+\rho$ is at most $C\log n$ with probability $1-C/n^2$ and in expectation.
nodes.label: thm:crr-coin

nodes.statement_short: Target-set duality, per-vertex infection probability summed with the spectral lemma, then the phase theorems with a suitable $c$.
nodes.statement: Both coin processes are target-set processes, whose duality is proved as Theorem~4. A vertex $u\ne v$ is infected with probability $(1+\rho)P_u-\rho P_u^2$, $P_u=d_A(u)/r$; sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}. Then Theorems~\ref{thm:crr-phases} to~\ref{thm:crr-cobra} apply with $c=\min(1,\rho_0(1-\max(\lambda_0,0)))$, and $128\sqrt{\log n/n}\le c$ for $n$ large.

nodes.name: Duality
nodes.statement: Both coin processes are target-set processes, whose duality is proved as Theorem~4.
nodes.statement_short: Coin processes are target-set processes, so duality holds.

nodes.name: Growth
nodes.statement: A vertex $u\ne v$ is infected with probability $(1+\rho)P_u-\rho P_u^2$, $P_u=d_A(u)/r$; sum and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:crr-spectral}.
nodes.statement_short: Per-vertex infection probability summed with the spectral lemma.

nodes.name: Apply phase theorems
nodes.statement: Then Theorems~\ref{thm:crr-phases} to~\ref{thm:crr-cobra} apply with $c=\min(1,\rho_0(1-\max(\lambda_0,0)))$, and $128\sqrt{\log n/n}\le c$ for $n$ large.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the phase and cover theorems with suitable $c$.

nodes.name: Median dynamics
nodes.origin_citation: Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011
nodes.statement_short: Each node adopts the median of its own value and two uniformly sampled values; with two values this is 2-Choices.
nodes.statement: Values lie in a linear order. In a round every node samples two nodes uniformly at random (independently, with replacement) and adopts the median of its own value and the two sampled values. With two values this is 2-Choices: a node keeps its value unless both samples hold the other one.
nodes.label: def:median

nodes.name: Threshold reduction
nodes.statement_short: Thresholding the median process at any value gives the binary median process (2-Choices) on the same samples.
conclusions: The median commutes with monotone maps
for every threshold $\theta$ the indicator of $\{x_v\ge\theta\}$ evolves, round by round and for the same samples, as the binary median process
nodes.statement: The median commutes with monotone maps; hence for every threshold $\theta$ the indicator of $\{x_v\ge\theta\}$ evolves, round by round and for the same samples, as the binary median process.
nodes.label: thm:threshold

nodes.statement_short: Write the median via min and max, which commute with monotone maps.
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{med}(a,b,c)=\max(\min(a,b),\min(\max(a,b),c))$, and monotone maps commute with $\min$ and $\max$.

nodes.name: Validity, range, consensus
nodes.statement_short: Median dynamics preserves validity and range, consensus is fixed and reached almost surely.
conclusions: Every new value is a current value
values stay within any interval containing all current values
consensus configurations are fixed
consensus is reached almost surely
nodes.statement: Every new value is a current value, values stay within any interval containing all current values, consensus configurations are fixed, and consensus is reached almost surely.
nodes.label: thm:basic

nodes.statement_short: Median is one of its arguments; a positive-probability round gives consensus; apply the shared absorption theorem.
nodes.statement: The median is one of its arguments; the round in which every node samples node $0$ twice gives consensus and has positive probability; conclude with the shared absorption theorem.

nodes.name: Binary expectation
nodes.statement_short: With two values, the expected number of true nodes after one round is $n(3p^2-2p^3)$.
assumptions: With two values and a fraction $p$ of \texttt{true}
conclusions: the expected number of \texttt{true} after one round is $n(3p^2-2p^3)$
nodes.statement: With two values and a fraction $p$ of \texttt{true}, the expected number of \texttt{true} after one round is $n(3p^2-2p^3)$, the same cubic as for 3-Majority.
nodes.label: thm:expect

nodes.statement_short: Count per-node transition probabilities: true stays unless both samples false, false switches iff both true.
nodes.statement: A \texttt{true} node stays unless both samples are \texttt{false}, a \texttt{false} node switches iff both samples are \texttt{true}.

nodes.name: 2-Choices, w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: 2-Choices from a gap $128\sqrt{n\log n}$ reaches consensus in $\lceil128\log n\rceil$ rounds w.p. $\ge1-128/n$.
assumptions: the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $128\sqrt{n\log n}$
conclusions: all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-128/n$
nodes.statement: If $\log n\ge 128$ and the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $128\sqrt{n\log n}$, all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-128/n$.
nodes.label: thm:whp

nodes.statement_short: Three phases: Bernstein-driven gap growth, minority shrinkage, a final Markov round; combined via the nested-phases lemma.
nodes.statement: Phases as in the plurality package: while it is small, the gap grows by a factor $5/4$ per phase except with probability $O(n^{-2})$ (Bernstein); then the minority shrinks by $7/8$ per phase down to $O(\log n)$; a final round reaches consensus except with probability $O(n^{-1/2})$ (Markov). The phases are combined with the nested-phases lemma of the shared layer. The threshold $\log n\ge128$, i.e.\ $n\ge e^{128}$, comes from these crude constants.

nodes.name: Phases
nodes.statement: Phases as in the plurality package: while it is small, the gap grows by a factor $5/4$ per phase except with probability $O(n^{-2})$ (Bernstein); then the minority shrinks by $7/8$ per phase down to $O(\log n)$; a final round reaches consensus except with probability $O(n^{-1/2})$ (Markov).
nodes.statement_short: Gap growth, minority shrinkage, final Markov round.

nodes.name: Combine phases
nodes.statement: The phases are combined with the nested-phases lemma of the shared layer. The threshold $\log n\ge128$, i.e.\ $n\ge e^{128}$, comes from these crude constants.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the nested-phases lemma; constants explain $\log n\ge128$.

nodes.name: 2-Choices from any start
nodes.statement_short: Binary 2-Choices reaches consensus from any configuration in $O(\log n)$ rounds except with probability $O(1/n)$.
conclusions: all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, from every binary configuration (possibly perfectly balanced) all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$.
nodes.label: thm:binary-any

nodes.statement_short: Escape: an exponential potential of the gap contracts in expectation (Hoeffding away from balance, Paley-Zygmund near it), then the large-gap theorem finishes.
nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{18}$ and write $g$ for the number of \texttt{true} nodes minus the number of \texttt{false} nodes. \emph{Escape:} the potential $e^{-|g|/(256\sqrt n)}$ contracts in expectation by $e^{-1/65536}$ per round, up to an additive error $e^{1/131072-\sqrt n/512}$: away from balance by Hoeffding's lemma applied at every node, near balance because the next gap has variance at least $n/10$, so by Paley--Zygmund it leaves $[-\sqrt n/4,\sqrt n/4]$ with probability at least $9/64$. Iterating over $\lceil 2^{17}\log n\rceil$ rounds and applying Markov's inequality, $|g|\ge 128\sqrt{n\log n}$ except with probability $2/n$. \emph{Consensus:} Theorem~\ref{thm:whp}, applied to the configuration or to its flip, finishes within $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability $128/n$.

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{18}$ and write $g$ for the number of \texttt{true} nodes minus the number of \texttt{false} nodes.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $C$ and the gap $g$.

nodes.name: Escape
nodes.statement: \emph{Escape:} the potential $e^{-|g|/(256\sqrt n)}$ contracts in expectation by $e^{-1/65536}$ per round, up to an additive error $e^{1/131072-\sqrt n/512}$: away from balance by Hoeffding's lemma applied at every node, near balance because the next gap has variance at least $n/10$, so by Paley--Zygmund it leaves $[-\sqrt n/4,\sqrt n/4]$ with probability at least $9/64$. Iterating over $\lceil 2^{17}\log n\rceil$ rounds and applying Markov's inequality, $|g|\ge 128\sqrt{n\log n}$ except with probability $2/n$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential potential contracts; Markov gives a large gap w.h.p.

nodes.name: Consensus
nodes.statement: \emph{Consensus:} Theorem~\ref{thm:whp}, applied to the configuration or to its flip, finishes within $\lceil 128\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability $128/n$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the 2-Choices w.h.p. theorem.

nodes.name: Reduction to two values
nodes.statement_short: A failure bound $\varepsilon$ for binary configurations gives $(m-1)\varepsilon$ for $m$ distinct values.
assumptions: every binary configuration fails to reach consensus within $T$ rounds with probability at most $\varepsilon$
conclusions: a configuration with $m$ distinct values fails with probability at most $(m-1)\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: If every binary configuration fails to reach consensus within $T$ rounds with probability at most $\varepsilon$, then a configuration with $m$ distinct values fails with probability at most $(m-1)\varepsilon$.
nodes.label: thm:of-binary

nodes.statement_short: Non-consensus implies a non-consensus threshold configuration; union bound over $m-1$ thresholds.
nodes.statement: If a run has not reached consensus, two nodes hold values $a<b$, and the threshold configuration $\{x_v\ge b\}$, which follows the same rounds by Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold}, has not reached consensus either. Take a union bound over the $m-1$ thresholds above the minimum value.

nodes.name: Consensus from any configuration (Theorem 1 of Doerr et al., without adversary)
nodes.origin_citation: Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011 (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement_short: The median dynamics reaches consensus from any configuration in $O(\log n)$ rounds except with probability $O(1/n)$.
assumptions: every configuration with values in a linear order (any number of distinct values)
conclusions: all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, from every configuration with values in a linear order (any number of distinct values) all nodes agree after $\lceil C\log n\rceil$ rounds except with probability at most $C/n$. This is Theorem~1 of Doerr et al.\ without the adversary.
nodes.label: thm:any

nodes.statement_short: Amplify the binary bound by three blocks of rounds, then union bound over at most $n-1$ thresholds.
nodes.statement: Consensus is absorbing, so three blocks of $\lceil C_0\log n\rceil$ rounds turn the binary failure bound $C_0/n$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-any} into $(C_0/n)^3$. The union bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:of-binary} over at most $n-1$ thresholds gives $n(C_0/n)^3\le (3C_0+3)/n$, since $C_0^3\le n$ when $\log n\ge 3C_0+3$.

nodes.name: Fast binary consensus from a large gap
nodes.statement_short: From a gap $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$ 2-Choices finishes in $O(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
assumptions: the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$
conclusions: all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$, if the \texttt{true} nodes outnumber the \texttt{false} ones by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$, all nodes hold \texttt{true} after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:binary-fast

nodes.statement_short: Chain one-round moves through four segments (gap growth, minority halving, quadratic shrinkage, finish) with a union bound.
nodes.statement: Take $C=128$ and chain one-round moves, each failing with probability at most $n^{-2}$, through four segments: the gap grows by a factor $5/4$ per round until the minority is below $n/4$ ($O(\log(n/\Delta))$ rounds); six rounds bring the minority below $n/8$; it then shrinks quadratically, $m\mapsto\approx 3m^2/n$ (Bernstein), down to $512\log n$ ($O(\log\log n)$ rounds); eight more rounds give consensus. Consensus is absorbing, so the remaining rounds are harmless, and a union bound over the rounds gives the failure probability.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: Margins around a value
nodes.statement_short: If a value $v$ has margin $\Delta$ on both sides, all nodes hold $v$ after $O(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
assumptions: for a value $v$, the nodes holding a value $\ge v$ outnumber those holding a value $<v$ by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$
symmetrically the nodes holding a value $\le v$ outnumber those holding a value $>v$ by at least $\Delta$
conclusions: all nodes hold $v$ after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-2C/n$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if, for a value $v$, the nodes holding a value $\ge v$ outnumber those holding a value $<v$ by at least $\Delta\ge C\sqrt{n\log n}$, and symmetrically the nodes holding a value $\le v$ outnumber those holding a value $>v$ by at least $\Delta$, then all nodes hold $v$ after $\lceil C(\log(n/\Delta)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-2C/n$.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:median-fast

nodes.statement_short: Both threshold indicators at $v$ follow 2-Choices; apply the fast binary theorem to each and union bound.
nodes.statement: The indicators of $\{x_u\ge v\}$ and of $\{x_u\le v\}$ both evolve as 2-Choices with the same samples (the second because the median is self-dual), with gaps the two margins. When both reach consensus on \texttt{true}, all nodes hold $v$; conclude with Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-fast} (with the same $C=128$) and a union bound.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: Odd number of equally supported values (odd case of Theorem 21)
nodes.origin_citation: Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011 (Theorem 21, odd case)
nodes.statement_short: With $2k+1$ equally supported values the middle one wins within $O(\log(2k+1)+\log\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
assumptions: the nodes hold $2k+1$ distinct values, each held by $n/(2k+1)$ nodes, and $C(2k+1)\sqrt{n\log n}\le n$
conclusions: the middle value is held by all nodes after $\lceil C(\log(2k+1)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$: if the nodes hold $2k+1$ distinct values, each held by $n/(2k+1)$ nodes, and $C(2k+1)\sqrt{n\log n}\le n$, then the middle value is held by all nodes after $\lceil C(\log(2k+1)+\log\log n)\rceil$ rounds with probability at least $1-C/n$. This is the deterministic core of the odd case of Theorem~21 of Doerr et al.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast
nodes.label: thm:odd-split

nodes.statement_short: Both margins equal $n/(2k+1)$; apply the margins theorem.
nodes.statement: Both margins around the middle value equal $n/(2k+1)\ge C_0\sqrt{n\log n}$, and $\log(n/\Delta)=\log(2k+1)$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:median-fast} with $C=2C_0$.
nodes.section: 51 Many values: the middle one wins fast

nodes.name: Two-sample voting on a graph
nodes.statement_short: Each vertex samples two neighbours and adopts the median of its own and their opinions; defines minority $B$ and edge counts $E(S,T)$.
nodes.statement: On a simple graph $G$, in a round every vertex samples two neighbours independently and uniformly at random (with replacement) and adopts the median of its own opinion and the two sampled ones; with two opinions it adopts the sampled opinion when the two samples agree. For a majority opinion $a$, the minority $B$ is the set of vertices holding another opinion. $E(S,T)$ is the number of ordered pairs $(u,v)\in S\times T$ of adjacent vertices, so $E(S,S)=2|E(S)|$.
nodes.label: def:graph-voting

nodes.name: Second eigenvalue $\lambda_G$
nodes.statement: For a $d$-regular graph, $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ are the eigenvalues of the transition matrix $P=A/d$ and $\lambda_G=\max\{\lambda_2,|\lambda_n|\}$.
nodes.label: def:lambdaG

nodes.name: Expander mixing lemma
nodes.statement_short: Edge counts between vertex sets deviate from $d|S||T|/n$ by at most $\lambda_G d\sqrt{|S||T|}$.
assumptions: every $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph and for all vertex sets $S,T$
conclusions: $|E(S,T)-d|S||T|/n|\le\lambda_G\,d\sqrt{|S||T|}$
nodes.statement: On every $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph and for all vertex sets $S,T$, $|E(S,T)-d|S||T|/n|\le\lambda_G\,d\sqrt{|S||T|}$.
nodes.label: lem:eml

nodes.statement_short: Eigenbasis expansion of $1_S\cdot P1_T$ and Cauchy-Schwarz; trivial bound when $\lambda_G\ge1$.
nodes.statement: Expand $1_S\cdot P1_T=\sum_k\mu_k s_kt_k$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis. If $\lambda_G<1$, every eigenvector other than the top one has eigenvalue at most $\lambda_2<1$, hence is orthogonal to the all-ones vector, which is fixed by $P$; so the top term is $|S||T|/n$, and Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the others by $\lambda_G\sqrt{|S||T|}$. If $\lambda_G\ge1$, both $E(S,T)$ and $d|S||T|/n$ lie in $[0,d\sqrt{|S||T|}]$.

nodes.name: Eigen-expansion
nodes.statement: Expand $1_S\cdot P1_T=\sum_k\mu_k s_kt_k$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis.
nodes.statement_short: Expand in an orthonormal eigenbasis.

nodes.name: Case lambda < 1
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_G<1$, every eigenvector other than the top one has eigenvalue at most $\lambda_2<1$, hence is orthogonal to the all-ones vector, which is fixed by $P$; so the top term is $|S||T|/n$, and Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the others by $\lambda_G\sqrt{|S||T|}$.
nodes.statement_short: Top term exact, others bounded via Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Case lambda >= 1
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_G\ge1$, both $E(S,T)$ and $d|S||T|/n$ lie in $[0,d\sqrt{|S||T|}]$.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial bound.

nodes.name: Small sets are sparse
nodes.statement_short: On good expanders, small vertex sets span few edges.
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_G\le 3/5-\varepsilon$ and $|S|\le\varepsilon n$, then $E(S,S)\le (3/5)\,d|S|$.
nodes.label: lem:sparse

nodes.statement_short: Expander mixing lemma with $T=S$.
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:eml} with $T=S$, $E(S,S)\le d|S|^2/n+\lambda_Gd|S|\le(\varepsilon+3/5-\varepsilon)d|S|$.

nodes.name: One round of two-sample voting (Lemma 5 at alpha=3/10)
nodes.statement_short: If supersets of the minority are sparse, one round shrinks the minority by $24/25$ in expectation and by $49/50$ w.h.p.
assumptions: every superset $S\supseteq B$ with $|S|\le(1+1/\alpha)|B|$ spans at most $\alpha d|S|$ edges
conclusions: after one round $\mathbb E|B'|\le(1-(1-2\alpha)(1-3\alpha))|B|=(24/25)|B|$
$|B'|\le(49/50)|B|$ with probability at least $1-e^{-|B|/4850}$
nodes.statement: If every superset $S\supseteq B$ with $|S|\le(1+1/\alpha)|B|$ spans at most $\alpha d|S|$ edges, then after one round $\mathbb E|B'|\le(1-(1-2\alpha)(1-3\alpha))|B|=(24/25)|B|$, and $|B'|\le(49/50)|B|$ with probability at least $1-e^{-|B|/4850}$.
nodes.label: lem:phase2

nodes.statement_short: Compute the expected new minority via neighbour fractions, bound with Cauchy-Schwarz, a chord bound and sparsity; Chernoff for concentration.
nodes.statement:
Let $p_v$ be the fraction of neighbours of $v$ in $B$ and $y=\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)$, which equals $\sum_{v
otin B}p_v$ by double counting. Then $\mathbb E|B'|=\sum_{v
otin B}p_v^2+\sum_{v\in B}(1-(1-p_v)^2)$. Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2\ge y^2/|B|$. With $C=\{v
otin B:p_v>3/10\}$, the chord bound $p^2\le(3/10)p+(p-3/10)^+$ and the sparsity of $B\cup C$ (which has at most $(13/3)|B|$ vertices) give $\sum_{v
otin B}p_v^2\le(3/10)y+(y-(2/5)|B|)/2$. Altogether $\mathbb E|B'|\le(24/25)|B|-(y-(2/5)|B|)^2/|B|$. The new minority is a sum of independent indicators; the multiplicative Chernoff bound with mean bound $(24/25)m$ and $\delta=1/48$ gives $\Pr(|B'|\ge(49/50)m)\le e^{-m/4850}$ for every $m\ge|B|$.

nodes.name: Expected minority
nodes.statement: Let $p_v$ be the fraction of neighbours of $v$ in $B$ and $y=\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)$, which equals $\sum_{v\notin B}p_v$ by double counting. Then $\mathbb E|B'|=\sum_{v\notin B}p_v^2+\sum_{v\in B}(1-(1-p_v)^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce neighbour fractions and write $\mathbb E|B'|$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2\ge y^2/|B|$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on $\sum(1-p_v)^2$.

nodes.name: Chord and sparsity
nodes.statement: With $C=\{v\notin B:p_v>3/10\}$, the chord bound $p^2\le(3/10)p+(p-3/10)^+$ and the sparsity of $B\cup C$ (which has at most $(13/3)|B|$ vertices) give $\sum_{v\notin B}p_v^2\le(3/10)y+(y-(2/5)|B|)/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\sum p_v^2$ outside $B$ via the chord bound and sparsity.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Altogether $\mathbb E|B'|\le(24/25)|B|-(y-(2/5)|B|)^2/|B|$.
nodes.statement_short: Expected minority at most $(24/25)|B|$.

nodes.name: Chernoff
nodes.statement: The new minority is a sum of independent indicators; the multiplicative Chernoff bound with mean bound $(24/25)m$ and $\delta=1/48$ gives $\Pr(|B'|\ge(49/50)m)\le e^{-m/4850}$ for every $m\ge|B|$.
nodes.statement_short: Multiplicative Chernoff bound gives the tail.

nodes.name: Two-sample voting on expanders (Theorem 4 of Cooper-Elsässer-Radzik)
nodes.statement_short: On expanders with $\lambda_G\le3/5-\varepsilon$, two-sample voting eliminates a minority of size $\le(\varepsilon/5)n$ in $O(\log n)$ rounds w.h.p.
assumptions: the minority have size at most $(\varepsilon/5)n$
conclusions: After $T$ rounds every vertex holds the majority opinion except with probability at most $(24/25)^T|B|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$
For $T=\lceil C\log n\rceil$ with $C=25000$ the failure probability is at most $1/n+(C\log n+1)e^{-\varepsilon n/C}$
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a $d$-regular $n$-vertex graph with $d>0$ and $\lambda_G\le3/5-\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon>0$, and let the minority have size at most $(\varepsilon/5)n$. After $T$ rounds every vertex holds the majority opinion except with probability at most $(24/25)^T|B|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$. For $T=\lceil C\log n\rceil$ with $C=25000$ the failure probability is at most $1/n+(C\log n+1)e^{-\varepsilon n/C}$, which tends to $0$ for fixed $\varepsilon$.
nodes.label: thm:expander

nodes.statement_short: Minority stays in the sparse regime and contracts in expectation each round; induction on $T$ for a bounded observable.
nodes.statement: While $|B|\le(\varepsilon/5)n$, every superset of $B$ of size at most $(13/3)|B|\le\varepsilon n$ is sparse (Lemma~\ref{lem:sparse}), so by Lemma~\ref{lem:phase2} the expected minority contracts by $24/25$ in every round and one round leaves this region with probability at most $e^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$ (take $m=(\varepsilon/5)n$). By induction on $T$, a $[0,1]$-valued observable bounded by the potential $|B|$ in the region has expectation at most $(24/25)^T|B_0|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$; apply it to the indicator of not being in consensus. For the $O(\log n)$ form, $(24/25)^T\le e^{-T/25}\le n^{-2}$ and $|B_0|\le n$.

nodes.name: Contraction
nodes.statement: While $|B|\le(\varepsilon/5)n$, every superset of $B$ of size at most $(13/3)|B|\le\varepsilon n$ is sparse (Lemma~\ref{lem:sparse}), so by Lemma~\ref{lem:phase2} the expected minority contracts by $24/25$ in every round and one round leaves this region with probability at most $e^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$ (take $m=(\varepsilon/5)n$).
nodes.statement_short: Sparsity and one-round lemma give contraction in the region.

nodes.name: Induction
nodes.statement: By induction on $T$, a $[0,1]$-valued observable bounded by the potential $|B|$ in the region has expectation at most $(24/25)^T|B_0|+Te^{-\varepsilon n/24250}$; apply it to the indicator of not being in consensus.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $T$ bounds the failure observable.

nodes.name: Log form
nodes.statement: For the $O(\log n)$ form, $(24/25)^T\le e^{-T/25}\le n^{-2}$ and $|B_0|\le n$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $T$ to make $(24/25)^T\le n^{-2}$.

nodes.statement: Throughout, $a$ is the majority opinion, $A$ and $B$ are the numbers of vertices holding $a$ and not holding $a$, $n=A+B$, and primes denote the values after one round.
nodes.name: Majority and minority counts $A$, $B$
nodes.section: 53 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance

nodes.name: Imbalance and flows
nodes.statement_short: Defines imbalance $\nu$, parameter $\eta$, the flows $\Delta_{BA},\Delta_{AB}$ of a round, and the Phase I length $T_1(\nu,c)$.
nodes.statement:
The imbalance is $
u=(A-B)/n$, and $\eta=\alpha n/\sqrt{AB}$ for a parameter $\alpha$. The flows of a round are $\Delta_{BA}$, the number of vertices of $B$ that hold $a$ after the round, and $\Delta_{AB}$, the number of vertices of $A$ that no longer hold $a$; so $B'+\Delta_{BA}=B+\Delta_{AB}$. The length of Phase~I is $T_1(
u,c)=\ceil{\log_{5/4}(1/(2
u))}+\ceil{\log_{4/3}(1/(4c))}$.
nodes.section: 53 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: def:cer-imbalance

nodes.name: Mixing hypothesis
nodes.statement_short: Edge counts between large disjoint sets are close to $d|X||Y|/n$ up to $\alpha d\sqrt{|X||Y|}$.

nodes.statement_short: Write flows via neighbour fractions; Cauchy-Schwarz plus mixing for the first, layer-cake sum over dyadic level sets for the second.
nodes.statement: Let $p_v$ be the fraction of neighbours of $v$ in $B$. A vertex of $B$ adopts $a$ with probability $(1-p_v)^2$ and a vertex of $A$ leaves $a$ with probability $p_v^2$, so $\E\Delta_{BA}=\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2$ and $\E\Delta_{AB}=\sum_{v\in A}p_v^2$. For the first, Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum_{v\in B}(1-p_v)^2\ge(E(B,A)/d)^2/B$, and the mixing hypothesis gives $E(B,A)\ge(dAB/n)(1-\eta)$. For the second, the hypothesis bounds the size of $\{v\in A:p_v\ge(1+2^j\eta)B/n\}$ by $A/4^j$; summing $p_v^2$ as a layer cake over these sets, up to the $m$ with $4^m\le n^2/(\eta B^2)<4^{m+1}$, gives the bound, since $(1+3m)\eta\le5$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 of the paper needs a major correction
nodes.statement_short: Counterexample on the complete graph: with constant initial difference the majority wins only with probability tending to $1/2$, so Theorem 2 fails as stated.
nodes.statement:
The paper states Theorem~2 with success probability $1-o(1)$ whenever $
u_0\ge K\lambda_G$, on every $d$-regular graph. Its proof applies Lemma~2 with $\alpha=\lambda_G$, whose failure probability is $e^{-\Theta(\lambda_G^2n)}$; this is not $o(1)$ when $\lambda_G$ is of order $1/\sqrt n$ or smaller. On the complete graph, $\lambda_G=1/(n-1)$, so a constant difference $A-B\in\{K+2,K+3\}$ satisfies the hypothesis for $n\ge K+3$; the first round produces fluctuations of order $\sqrt n$ in $A-B$, and by symmetry the initial majority then wins with probability tending to $1/2$. Theorem~ef{thm:cer-theorem2} is the corrected statement: it keeps the hypothesis $
u_0\ge K\lambda_G$ and bounds the failure probability in terms of $
u_0^2n$, which tends to $0$ once $
u_0^2n$ is large compared with $\log\log n$ (\href{https://github.com/formal-dynamics/leanamics/blob/main/median/FORMALIZATION_DIFFERENCES.md#theorem-2-of-the-paper-needs-a-major-correction}{details}).
nodes.section: 53 Two-sample voting from a small imbalance
nodes.label: rem:cer-correction

nodes.name: Adaptive adversary
nodes.origin_citation: Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011
nodes.statement_short: An $F$-bounded adaptive adversary recolours at most $F$ nodes after each median round; defines perturbed runs and almost stable consensus.
nodes.statement: An adversary maps the list of rounds played so far (the current one last) and the output of the median rule in the current round to a new configuration; it is $F$-bounded if it recolours at most $F$ nodes, and it uses values of $S$ if every value it writes lies in $S$. The run against the adversary applies, in every round, the median rule and then the adversary. More generally, a perturbed run is any function of the rounds played so far that starts at $x$ and, after every round, differs from the output of the median rule in at most $F$ nodes. A configuration is in almost consensus on $b$ with $K$ exceptions if at most $K$ nodes hold a value other than $b$; almost stable consensus during the times $T_0,\dots,T_0+H$ means almost consensus on the same value $b$ at all these times.
nodes.section: 54 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.label: def:adversary

nodes.name: 2-Choices against an adaptive adversary
nodes.origin_citation: Doerr, Goldberg, Minder, Sauerwald, Scheideler, SPAA 2011 (Theorem 10, 2009 version)
nodes.statement_short: Binary 2-Choices reaches almost stable consensus with $O(F+\log n)$ exceptions within $O(\log n)$ rounds against any $F$-bounded adversary.
assumptions: every binary configuration, every perturbed run with budget $F$ (in particular, the run against every $F$-bounded adversary) and every $H\ge0$
conclusions: almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(C\log n+H)/n^2$
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $\log n\ge C$ and $CF\le\sqrt n$, for every binary configuration, every perturbed run with budget $F$ (in particular, the run against every $F$-bounded adversary) and every $H\ge0$, almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(C\log n+H)/n^2$. This is the two-value case (Theorem~10 of the 2009 version) of the main theorem of Doerr et al.
nodes.section: 54 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary
nodes.label: thm:binary-adv

nodes.statement_short: Escape via the contracting exponential potential, robust to recolourings; then chained one-round growth and saturation moves with a union bound.
nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{20}$, so $F\le\sqrt n/1024$, and let $g$ be the gap and $K=\max(16F,1024\log n)$. Recolouring $F$ nodes moves $g$ by at most $2F$ and the minority by at most $F$. \emph{Escape:} the potential $e^{-|g|/(256\sqrt n)}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-any} grows by at most $e^{1/131072}$ under the recolourings, so it still contracts by $e^{-1/131072}$ per round up to an additive $e^{1/65536-\sqrt n/512}$; after $\lceil 2^{19}\log n\rceil$ rounds Markov's inequality gives $|g|\ge 128\sqrt{n\log n}$ except with probability $2/n^2$. \emph{Growth and saturation} (for $g>0$; otherwise flip): a chain of one-round moves, each failing with probability at most $n^{-2}$ for every recolouring, along sets indexed by time: the gap grows from $G$ to $\min(9G/8,17n/32)$ (Hoeffding: $5G/4$ before the recolouring), then the minority shrinks from $t$ to $\max(15t/16,K)$ (Bernstein: $\max(7t/8,512\log n)$ before the recolouring) and stays below $K$. A union bound over the rounds of the chain and of the window gives the bound.
nodes.section: 54 Almost stable consensus against an adaptive adversary

assumptions: $S$ be a set of $m$ legal values containing the values of a configuration $x$
Against every $F$-bounded adversary that only writes values of $S$, and for every $H\ge0$
conclusions: almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(m-1)(C\log n+H)/n^2$

Against every $F$-bounded adversary that only writes values of $S$, and for every $H\ge0$, almost stable consensus with $C(F+\log n)$ exceptions holds during the times $\lceil C\log n\rceil,\dots,\lceil C\log n\rceil+H$, except with probability at most $(m-1)(C\log n+H)/n^2$.

nodes.statement_short: Thresholds of the run are perturbed 2-Choices runs; combine their almost-consensus values into one value $w$; union bound over thresholds.
nodes.statement: Take $C=2^{20}$. All values of the run lie in $S$. For every legal value $b$, the threshold $u\mapsto[b\le x_u]$ of the run is a perturbed run of 2-Choices with the same budget, because the median commutes with monotone maps and thresholding does not increase the Hamming distance. If, for every legal $b$ above the minimum $m_0$, the threshold run stays in almost consensus on some $c_b$ with $K$ exceptions, let $w$ be the largest legal value with $w=m_0$ or $c_w=\texttt{true}$: the nodes below $w$ are exceptions of the threshold at $w$, and the nodes above $w$ are exceptions of the threshold at the next legal value, so the run is in almost consensus on $w$ with $2K$ exceptions. Conclude with the internal bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-adv} and a union bound over the $m-1$ thresholds.
